subject: Trading
title: Log vs. Linear Scale
description: One-minute skill: Log vs. Linear Scale.

hook.text: Amazon went from $5 to $3,000. On a linear chart, the early years look flat. On a log chart, growth is clear.

buildup.text: Linear charts plot equal dollar distances. A $10 move always looks the same, whether from $10 or $1,000.

discovery.text: Log charts plot equal percentage distances. A 100% gain always looks the same, regardless of price level.

twist.text: Using linear scale on long-term charts hides early price action and exaggerates recent moves.

climax.text: Log scale is essential for long-term analysis. Most professionals default to it for charts spanning years.

quiz.question: When should you use a logarithmic chart scale?
options: For long-term charts where percentage moves matter more
